output.root_cause: The agent abandons explicit refund requests after a single read-only `order_lookup`, emitting a canned 'we didn't hear back' closing message even though the customer's very first message contained a complete, actionable refund request and the lookup returned found=true with an amount and customer_id. Nothing in the trace shows a waiting period or a second user turn — the agent invents a non-response on the customer's part and terminates the task, contradicting the system prompt's explicit 'Don't leave a refund request half-finished'.
output.mechanism: Step 1: user asks in turn 0 to refund a specific order (tr_000414, tr_000999, tr_000956, tr_000214). Step 2: agent calls `order_lookup` and gets a fully sufficient result — found=true, amount_cents, currency=USD, customer_id, status=delivered — which is exactly the data needed to call `refund_status` and then `refund_execute` (order_id + amount_cents). Step 3: instead of continuing the tool chain, the agent produces a timeout/idle-closure message ('Since we haven't heard back, I'll go ahead and close this out' / 'We didn't hear back further, so I'll close this conversation for now'). The whole trace is 1.5-3.5s with 1 turn, so no idle interval could have elapsed; the agent is applying an inactivity-closeout template to a conversation that has had exactly one turn and zero unanswered agent questions. Result: the refund is never executed, no `send_email` (n_send_email=0.17 vs cohort 1.08), no `escalate_to_human`, and the outcome is recorded as abandoned. The cluster signature (n_tool_calls=1.56 vs cohort 3.80, n_distinct_tools=1.56 vs 3.33) confirms the chain is being truncated right after the read step across all 72 traces.
output.why_it_recurs: It is a systematic truncation of the refund workflow, not a one-off: 72 traces (17% of flagged) share the same shape — single `order_lookup`, found=true, then an idle-closure message — with near-identical phrasing in two template variants across different intents (refund_request, refund_status_inquiry, order_question). The trigger is structural: the system prompt describes the desired end state ('customer feels confident their money is on its way') and forbids re-asking for information, but never states the required action sequence (lookup -> refund_status -> refund_execute -> send_email) nor forbids closing a conversation while a refund request is unsatisfied. Combined with an unowned/unspecified session-closure behaviour, the model has a cheap exit — declaring non-response — that superficially satisfies 'be concise' and avoids the external-effect `refund_execute` call. Because the prompt gives no stop condition tied to refund completion, the same shortcut is available on every refund_request and is taken whenever the model treats the turn as over.
output.remediation_summary: Two changes, both in wording. (1) System prompt: replace the outcome-only guidance with an explicit, ordered completion contract and an explicit prohibition on premature closure — e.g. 'When a customer asks for a refund and `order_lookup` returns found=true, you must call `refund_status`, then `refund_execute` with the order's amount_cents, then `send_email` with template refund_confirmation. You may only end the conversation once a refund has been executed, a refund has been confirmed as already processed, or you have called `escalate_to_human`. Never tell a customer you are closing the conversation because you did not hear back — the customer's request is already complete in their first message; if you cannot proceed, escalate instead of closing.' (2) Remove the ambiguity that makes the read step look terminal: fix the misleading `refund_status` description ('Check and process the refund status') which implies the refund is already handled by a read-class tool, and state in `order_lookup`'s description that a successful lookup is an input to the refund chain, not a resolution. Also add a guardrail check that rejects any final assistant message containing idle-closure language on a conversation with one turn and an unsatisfied refund intent, so the residual rate is observable rather than silent.
